newsitem.title: THAILAND: Wall Street denies cash problems.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street denies cash problems.

text.p: Wall Street Finance and Securities Plc said on Friday that it did not have any cash problems and the company had issued only Euro convertible debentures worth 1.39 billion baht (US$56 million)
The company, in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand, denied a local media report that it was facing severe liquidity problems and had no reserves for redeeming debentures due soon.
Wall Street said its Euro convertible debentures were due for redemption in 2004 and all the debentures were offered to overseas investors without put option.
Finance companies have been hurt by rising interest rates in recent months due to a sustained liquidity crunch.
Some medium and small finance companies are facing cash-flow problems which arose from an extended bearish stock market and a troubled property sector.
Wall Street was trading at 12.50 baht at 0309 GMT on Friday, unchanged from Thursday.
